Options

Every option works as a JavaScript option in camelCase and as an attribute in kebab-case. Leave one out and you get the default; set one later with bot.set() or by changing the attribute, and the avatar eases into it.

<bot-avatar type="cat" face="mouth" hat="party" bow-tie accessory-color="#5b5bf7"></bot-avatar>
createBot('#agent', { type: 'cat', face: 'mouth', hat: 'party', bowTie: true, accessoryColor: '#5b5bf7' });

Opt-in behaviours for agents. Each loads its code the first time it's switched on, so the ones you don't use cost nothing.

socialbots on the same page glance at each otherfalse
tossdrag the avatar and throw itfalse
pettingstroke it with the pointer and it reactsfalse
soundssound effects; true or a volume 0–1false

Grouped options#

Flat options and grouped objects are interchangeable; groups are easier to read and write:

createBot('#agent', {
  type: 'cat',
  preset: 'teddy',
  fur: { length: 1.6, clumps: 0.6, pattern: 'stripes', color: '#8b5a2b', scale: 1.2 },
  light: { angle: 290, color: '#ffe7b3', fill: '#4c6fff', fillStrength: 0.4, rimColor: '#7ad7ff' },
  material: { roundness: 0.8, gloss: 0.4 },
  face: { eyes: { style: 'oval', iris: '#3b82f6' }, brows: 'soft', mouth: 'cat', freckles: true, expression: 'smug' },
  motion: { blinkRate: 1.4, breathing: 1.5, jump: { height: 0.5, spin: 2, squash: 1.3 } },
  wear: { hat: 'witch', ears: 'bunny', scarf: true, badge: 'AI', antennae: 'two' },
});

In HTML, groups take JSON. The face group is face-options, because face is the eyes/mouth switch:

<bot-avatar type="cat" fur='{"pattern":"spots"}' face-options='{"mouth":"cat"}'></bot-avatar>
GroupOptions
furlength, density, fuzz, curl, gravity, clumps, pattern, color, scale
lightangle, color, fill, fillStrength, rimColor, shadow, highlight, rim, spread
materialshading, roundness, gloss, depth
facefeatures (eyes/mouth), eyes: { style, size, gap, shine, iris }, brows, mouth, freckles, x, y, scale, blush, blushColor, ink, expression
motionspeed, turn, blinkRate, glanceRate, breathing, jiggle, whirl, whirlColor, jump: { every, height, time, spin, squash, stretch, lean }
wearhat, glasses, headphones, bowTie, color, scarf, scarfColor, badge, badgeColor, ears, antennae, accessories

DNA and identity#

Two ways to get a whole look from one string:

const code = bot.dna;                          // 'bot1.…': the whole design, URL-safe
createBot('#copy', { dna: code });             // the same bot again
createBot('#user', { identity: user.email });  // a stable look of its own for every id

Options you pass alongside dna, identity or preset win over theirs. DNA codes are what the studio shares and what crew pages are made of.

CSS variables#

<bot-avatar> reads colours from CSS where no attribute sets them: --bot-color, --bot-ink, --bot-accessory-color, --bot-blush-color, --bot-fur-color, --bot-light-color, --bot-fill-color, --bot-rim-color and --bot-iris-color. Call el.refresh() after changing them.

.team-red bot-avatar { --bot-color: #ff5c5c; --bot-accessory-color: #2b2833; }
